items.name: Humanist Perspective
items.plain_en: emphasizes free will and personal growth

items.name: Psychodynamic Perspective
items.plain_en: unconscious mind controls much thought and action

items.name: Biopsychology (or Neuroscience) Perspective
items.plain_en: explains behavior through biological processes

items.name: Evolutionary (or Darwinian) Perspective
items.plain_en: interprets behavior through natural selection

items.name: Behavioral Perspective
items.plain_en: explains behavior through conditioning

items.name: Cognitive Perspective
items.plain_en: studies how people interpret, process, and remember events

items.name: Social-Cultural (or Sociocultural) Perspective
items.plain_en: examines how culture shapes thoughts and behavior

items.name: Biopsychosocial Perspective
items.plain_en: combines biological, psychological, and social factors

items.name: eclectic
items.plain_en: combines multiple perspectives rather than one

items.name: Hindsight bias
items.plain_en: overestimates what one knew in advance

items.name: Confirmation bias
items.plain_en: favors information supporting preexisting ideas

items.name: Overconfidence
items.plain_en: overestimates the accuracy of one's beliefs

items.name: Applied research
items.plain_en: research with clear practical applications

items.name: Basic research
items.plain_en: explores questions without immediate practical application

items.name: Quantitative research
items.plain_en: measures variables with numbers

items.name: Qualitative research
items.plain_en: analyzes textual responses for key themes

items.name: Hypothesis
items.plain_en: states a relationship between two variables

items.name: Variables
items.plain_en: factors that can vary among participants

items.name: Experimental hypothesis
items.plain_en: dependent variable depends on independent variable

items.name: Independent variable
items.plain_en: variable the researcher manipulates

items.name: Dependent variable
items.plain_en: variable measured as the outcome

items.name: Theory
items.plain_en: explains phenomena and generates testable hypotheses

items.name: Falsifiable
items.plain_en: possible to gather data disproving it

items.name: Operational definitions
items.plain_en: explains how a variable will be measured

items.name: Validity
items.plain_en: measures what it is intended to measure

items.name: Reliability
items.plain_en: produces consistent, replicable results

items.name: Sampling
items.plain_en: process of selecting research participants

items.name: Population
items.plain_en: everyone who could possibly be selected

items.name: Representative sample
items.plain_en: sample reflecting the larger population

items.name: Random sampling
items.plain_en: every population member has equal selection chance

items.name: Convenience sampling
items.plain_en: uses easily accessible participants

items.name: Stratified sampling
items.plain_en: ensures sample matches population on criteria

items.name: Confounding variable
items.plain_en: extraneous difference affecting the dependent variable

items.name: Random assignment
items.plain_en: equal chance of placement into either group

items.name: Group matching
items.plain_en: groups matched on relevant criteria

items.name: Experimenter bias
items.plain_en: researcher unconsciously treats groups differently

items.name: Double-blind study
items.plain_en: neither participants nor researchers know group assignments

items.name: Single-blind study
items.plain_en: only participants unaware of group assignment

items.name: Demand characteristics
items.plain_en: cues revealing the study's purpose

items.name: Experimental group
items.plain_en: group receiving the treatment

items.name: Control group
items.plain_en: group receiving no treatment

items.name: Placebo method
items.plain_en: control group receives inactive but identical substance

items.name: Correlation
items.plain_en: relationship between two variables, not causation

items.name: Positive correlation
items.plain_en: one variable's presence predicts the other's

items.name: Negative correlation
items.plain_en: one variable's presence predicts the other's absence

items.name: Ex post facto (quasi-experimental) study
items.plain_en: quasi-experiment that cannot prove causation

items.name: Survey method
items.plain_en: asks people to fill out surveys

items.name: Likert scales
items.plain_en: statement rated by agreement level

items.name: Directionality problem
items.plain_en: cannot tell which variable came first

items.name: Spurious correlation
items.plain_en: false correlation caused by third variable

items.name: Naturalistic observation
items.plain_en: observing participants in natural habitat without interacting

items.name: Qualitative data
items.plain_en: open-ended written responses

items.name: Structured interview
items.plain_en: fixed questions asked in set order

items.name: Semistructured or unstructured interviews
items.plain_en: flexible interviews allowing follow-up questions

items.name: Case study method
items.plain_en: detailed picture of one participant

items.name: Science Practice 3—Data Analysis
items.plain_en: making inferences from numerical data

items.name: Descriptive statistics
items.plain_en: summarizes a set of data

items.name: Mean
items.plain_en: arithmetic average of all scores

items.name: Median
items.plain_en: central score in a distribution

items.name: Mode
items.plain_en: most frequently occurring score

items.name: Positively skewed distribution
items.plain_en: extreme high score causes positive skew

items.name: Negatively skewed distribution
items.plain_en: extreme low score causes negative skew

items.name: Range
items.plain_en: distance between highest and lowest scores

items.name: Standard deviation
items.plain_en: measures how spread out scores are

items.name: z-scores
items.plain_en: distance from mean in standard deviation units

items.name: Normal curve
items.plain_en: theoretical bell-shaped curve

items.name: Percentiles
items.plain_en: percentage scoring below a given score

items.name: Correlation
items.plain_en: measures the relationship between two variables

items.name: Positive correlation
items.plain_en: presence of one predicts the other

items.name: Negative correlation
items.plain_en: presence of one predicts the other's absence

items.name: Correlation coefficient
items.plain_en: statistic showing a correlation's strength

items.name: Scatterplot
items.plain_en: graphs pairs of values as points

items.name: Line of best fit
items.plain_en: line minimizing distances from scatterplot points

items.name: Inferential statistics
items.plain_en: applies sample findings to the population

items.name: Sampling error
items.plain_en: extent sample differs from population

items.name: p-value
items.plain_en: probability difference is due to chance

items.name: Statistical significance
items.plain_en: result unlikely due to chance

items.name: Practical significance
items.plain_en: how large an effect is

items.name: Replication
items.plain_en: repeating a study to verify results

items.name: Meta-analysis
items.plain_en: combines many studies into average effect

items.name: Peer review
items.plain_en: experts review papers before publication

items.name: Institutional review board (IRB)
items.plain_en: committee reviewing research ethics

items.name: Clear scientific purpose
items.plain_en: research must serve clear scientific aims

items.name: Least amount of suffering feasible
items.plain_en: minimize animal suffering

items.name: No coercion
items.plain_en: people choose to participate freely

items.name: Informed consent
items.plain_en: participants know and agree to participate

items.name: Confidentiality (or anonymity)
items.plain_en: protects participants' privacy

items.name: Risk
items.plain_en: avoid significant mental or physical harm

items.name: Debriefing
items.plain_en: explains study purpose afterward
